headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; Continue’s broad filesystem/MCP access can ingest Cognee outputs and sensitive support data by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, while Cognee handles documents, workflows, and support history. That creates a plausible path where Cognee-generated content is fed into Continue as trusted context. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so injection risk exists in default shared-workspace setups, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are copied into files or MCP payloads that Continue reads as instructions
IF Continue is connected to a shared workspace containing Cognee-generated content
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable MCP servers for Continue unless needed
Mark Cognee outputs as untrusted text in prompts
Add a manual review step before Continue acts on Cognee content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Continue reads and writes workspace files and can send context to a user-chosen model provider over broad egress. In a shared workspace, sensitive Cognee data can flow into Continue and then to third-party inference. The pairwise leakage path is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF Cognee stores sensitive support or finance data in files that Continue can read
IF Continue is configured to use a remote model provider for those files
mitigations: Move sensitive Cognee data to a separate directory
Use a local-only model provider in Continue
Restrict Continue to a non-sensitive workspace
Rotate any exposed model-provider API keys
requires-engineering: add workspace-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and Continue supports multiple instances with filesystem-shared state. Both can operate on the same host and workspace, so concurrent writes or state drift are plausible even though Continue does not modify git state. The overlap is real but narrower than high because the profiles do not show unrestricted git or database writes.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same workspace directory
IF Cognee persists session state into files that Continue also edits
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace
Serialize edits with a simple operator checklist
Back up the workspace before concurrent use
Disable one agent while the other is writing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP/tool outputs and workspace content, while Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations that may be treated as authoritative context. If Continue consumes Cognee output without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or actions. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, but the profiles do not show autonomous external actions, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Continue uses Cognee output as source material without human verification
IF MCP tool calls are approved based on Cognee-generated recommendations
mitigations: Require human review before tool approval
Ask Continue to cite source files before acting
Keep Cognee output in a separate notes file
Use a checklist to verify high-impact changes

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Continue handles workspace files and model-provider API keys. If the same sensitive data is placed into Continue’s remote model path, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Cognee’s support-data handling. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is routed from Cognee into Continue’s remote provider path
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Continue prompts
Use a local model provider for sensitive work
Document retention settings for both tools
Separate support-data and code-review workflows
